_comment: Virginia 2026 plan, Virginia Housing. The plan is the authority's regulation 13VAC10-180; competitive scoring is 13VAC10-180-60 E, PDF pp.13-20. Page numbers are PDF page indices and match the printed numbers. Virginia states no maximum score; it states a 300-point floor (200 for tax-exempt bond deals) below which an application is rejected. Several criteria are formulas rather than fixed values, and points_max records the cap the plan states for each.

track_totals.note: No maximum is stated. The operative figure is a floor: 'Any application that is assigned a total number of points less than a threshold amount of 300 points (200 points for developments financed with tax-exempt bonds ...) shall be rejected from further consideration.' Several criteria scale with a percentage rather than sitting at a fixed value, so a computed maximum here is the sum of stated caps and not a score any real project would reach.

groups.label: Deeper income limits against deeper rent limits
groups.source_quote: may not receive points under subdivision 7 b of this subsection
groups.note: Subdivision 7 a and 7 b are explicitly exclusive of each other. 7 a caps at 50; 7 b caps at 25, or 50 in low-income jurisdictions where the calculation is doubled.

groups.label: Extended affordability against a nonprofit purchase option
groups.source_quote: may not receive bonus points under subdivision 7 d of this subsection
groups.note: Subdivision 7 c (40 points for ten further years, 70 for twenty) and 7 d (60 points, plus 5 for a homeownership plan) are explicitly exclusive of each other.

criteria.quote: The applicant receives two points for each percentage point up to a maximum of 60 points

criteria.quote: EarthCraft Gold or higher certification
criteria.note: Or LEED, National Green Building Standard Silver or higher, or Enterprise Green Communities Criteria, with the architect certifying the design will meet it and a RESNET rater registered with an approved provider. The plan states points in this subdivision are not cumulative. Every development must separately meet a baseline energy standard: Energy Star for new construction, a 30% HERS improvement or HERS 80 for rehabilitation, HERS 95 for adaptive reuse.

did not

criteria.quote: 100 points multiplied by the percentage by which the total amount

criteria.note: 100 multiplied by the percentage of units both rent restricted to and occupied by households at or below 50% AMI, plus a point per percentage further restricted to 30% or 40% AMI up to 10 more, plus a point per percentage at or below 30% AMI without project-based rental assistance, up to 10 more. Units a locality requires to exceed 60% AMI are excluded from the calculation.
